** Major** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Guard `AbortSignal.any` for runtimes that lack it.** The peer package `@tanstack/ai` declares `node >=18`. `AbortSignal.any` is available only from Node 18.17.0 and 20.3.0. On Node 18.0–18.16 and 20.0–20.2, this line throws a `TypeError` when `timeoutMs` is positive and a caller signal is provided. Before this change, that combination did not call `AbortSignal.any`, so the failure is new for those runtimes. Check for `AbortSignal.any` before use. When it is absent, combine the caller signal and the timeout signal manually, as `packages/ai/src/utilities/activity-abort.ts` does. The composed signal must still abort when the caller aborts and when the timeout fires.

--- ** Major** · **Stability & Availability** · **Quick win** **Stop retries once the request signal aborts.** When `timeoutMs` is positive and a caller signal is present, the composed signal in `http.ts:273` aborts with a `TimeoutError` when the timeout fires. The retry predicate at lines 541-542 treats `TimeoutError` as retryable under the default `retryConnectionErrors: true`. Each attempt clones the same request (line 291). The clone keeps the aborted signal, so each attempt fails immediately. The loop then waits through backoff and repeats until `maxElapsedTime` expires. The retry loop never checks the request signal. A later caller abort does not stop this loop. The composed signal keeps the timeout reason, so the caller abort cannot change the outcome. Before this change, a caller abort on this path produced a non-retryable `AbortError`. A timeout-only request already has the same retry-on-aborted-request behavior. The caller-signal path now inherits it, and caller cancellation can no longer stop it. Once the request signal is aborted, the retry loop must not start another attempt. The backoff wait must also end when the signal aborts. Retries for recoverable failures must still run while the signal is live.
